person.name: Chris Theal
person.text: Chris Theal is Phytokana’s Founder, President, CEO and Director. He brings 25 + years of Alberta entrepreneurship, previously CFO of Velvet Energy (backed by CPPIB and Warburg Pincus), founder of an energy hedge fund and partner at Tristone Capital. A former Canadian Armed Forces officer, he also served as Past President of the Royal Military Colleges of Canada Foundation. He holds a BA in Economics (Distinction) from Royal Roads Military College, an MBA (Finance) from UBC, is a CFA charterholder (2000) and holds the ICD.D designation.

company.text: Phytokana Ingredients Inc. is an independent Alberta‑based innovator, processor and distributor of sustainable plant‑protein isolates sourced from yellow peas. It develops both conventional and organic protein concentrates and co‑products for the food & beverage sector. The company operates a head office in Calgary and a fractionation facility under construction in Strathmore, AB. It recently secured a **US$276,502 private‑placement** (SEC Form D) to fund the plant and future U.S. distribution. While it boasts a $450 M future offtake pipeline, it presently has **no U.S. office or staff**, planning U.S. market rollout after plant commissioning.

industry.title: Booming U.S. plant‑protein demand
industry.text: U.S. consumers are rapidly shifting toward plant‑based proteins, driving a surge in demand from food manufacturers. Aligning Phytokana’s high‑purity pea protein with this trend will require fast‑track buyer outreach—exactly where Gershon’s LinkedIn outbound expertise adds value.

talking_points: What is the targeted commercial launch date for the Strathmore facility?
Which U.S. food categories (e.g., beverages, snack bars, meat alternatives) are top priority for protein sales?
Do you have specific regulatory certifications (organic, non‑GMO) you need to emphasize for U.S. buyers?
How do you envision the sales model in the U.S.—direct to brand, distributor partnership, or joint‑venture?
Can we map the existing US investors to potential strategic customers or distributors?
What volume commitments are you seeking from early U.S. offtake partners?
Are there branding or packaging adaptations required for the U.S. market?
Do you have any pilot customers or test‑market results in North America?
What internal resources will you allocate to the U.S. go‑to‑market effort?
